scope: Read-only compile/crash diagnosis. No Quartus database opened, no RTL/SDC production edits, no system policy changes.

findings.finding: The observed GUI crash used Quartus 20.1, despite the user expecting 18.1.
evidence: Windows Application event 1000 at 2026-11-03T01:45:43.652+11:00 identifies C:/intelFPGA_lite/20.1/quartus/bin64/quartus.exe and QtCore4.dll
PartBDebug.map.summary and flow.rpt identify Quartus 20.1.0 Build 711. QPF still lists 18.1; LAST_QUARTUS_VERSION in QSF lists 20.1.0 Lite Edition.

findings.finding: The Windows crash signature is a GUI Qt callback exception, not a recorded quartus_fit.exe exception.
evidence: Faulting module QtCore4.dll 4.8.7.0; exception 0xc000041d; offset 0x111f6b; PID 0x20C84.
findings.limit: No quartus_fit.exe event appeared in the queried six-hour Application window. Absence of an event does not prove no child failure.

findings.finding: The prior 18.1 build reached routing and reported severe routing congestion with excessive hold-delay insertion.
evidence: Retained fit.qmsg contains 18.1 library references and timestamps from 00:43:59, preceding the 20.1 manual map.
00:49:26: approximately 10000 ns routing delay added for hold, 8.2% of available routing delay.
00:52:05: average interconnect usage 36%; peak 88% in X22_Y46 through X32_Y57.
01:09:53: message 188005 describes excessive demand and hold backoff; subsequent Warning 16684 predicts long routing runtime or substantial setup/hold failures.
findings.limit: The qmsg ends midrecord and is from the previous 18.1 attempt, not a complete report of the manual 20.1 run. No successful fitter result is available.

findings.finding: No Resource-Exhaustion-Detector or System event 2004 was found in the queried six-hour window.
findings.limit: This does not rule out transient memory pressure. Previous runtime sample already showed no fitter page-fault/I/O growth during the sampled stall.

findings.finding: WER archive directory/report was denied by Windows in both normal and approved escalated reads. Application event records were readable.
findings.limit: No ownership, ACL, account or policy changes were attempted.

findings.finding: Installed Quartus 18.1 set_min_delay/max_delay do not support -datapath_only or -ignore_clock_latency, and both include clock network latency.
evidence: sta_help_18_1.log: actual quartus_sta 18.1 help -cmd output, no project opened.

findings.finding: The wide CLOCK_50-to-PCLK bundled CDC min_delay 0 could force substantial artificial hold routing because unrelated-clock insertion differences remain in the analysis.
findings.nextTest: Use map timing diagnostics to identify the largest hold paths. In an experimental SDC only, replace the exact bundled-payload hold constraint with set_false_path -hold while retaining max_delay 20 ns; confirm setup bound remains. For Gray paths also confirm max_skew remains active, since installed help says false paths can affect skew.

nextControlledBuild: Preserve failed-run files and prevent concurrent GUI/CLI writes to the same compilation database.
Use a fresh isolated project build directory and explicit Quartus 18.1 executable paths.
Diagnose and correct only proved CDC hold constraints; do not blanket false-path synchronous logic or remove timing checks.
Capture fit.qmsg periodically because compile stdout can remain buffered during routing.
Require full fit, routed timing and fresh source-linked SOF before programming.
